title: 3DPLAM, 3D-Printed Lightweight Affordable Manifold for Microbial Water Quality Testing
description:
An open-source, 3D-printable membrane-filtration manifold for Escherichia coli quantification in drinking water. Three parts (base, funnel, filter support) print without support structures on a consumer FDM printer and, with a 100 mL syringe and a 0.45 um membrane filter, perform the membrane-filtration measurement used in WHO and UNICEF household drinking-water quality surveys.

Validated at 8 sample sites against a Millipore EZ-Fit stainless-steel manifold as the reference instrument, with 3 manifolds and 3 replicates per manifold per site (72 filtrations, 16 printed-vs-reference comparisons). 15 of 16 classifications are accepted under a 5 % WHO boundary-tolerance rule and 12 of 16 match the reference risk band exactly with no tolerance applied. 3DPLAM does not replace the EZ-Fit; its contribution is that the design is open and can be printed locally.

This archive contains the print-ready and editable geometry, the slicer profiles required for a gas-tight print, the full protocol and assembly documentation, the tidied validation and material-test datasets with a codebook, and the scripts that regenerate every figure.
